title: review step answer
description: A verdict, and every finding behind it, each carrying the grade that decides what it costs. Critical, Major and Minor send the work back and are fixed in this change; from review round 2 the driver moves each Minor to its screen's polish list instead; a Nit is dropped. A finding tagged pre-existing is in code this change did not introduce: it never blocks and never goes back to the builder; the driver hands it to the nightly sweep. The verdict is read off the grades, never typed beside them: SHIP with a Critical, Major or Minor that is not pre-existing, and BLOCKED with none, are both refused.

skills.description: Every skill invoked in this step. The driver cross-checks this against the Skill calls in the run log, so a claim here the log does not show is a failed step.

round.description: Which review round this is. The driver allows two; a blocking finding left after that keeps the change from merging.

panel.description: How the review was run: the reviewer skill, its effort, how many finder agents hunted and how many verifier agents voted. Present, every finding must carry its tag and its verifier's word.

findings.description: Everything this review raised, at every grade. One list, because the grade already says what each one costs — a second list saying the same thing is a second place for the two to disagree.

line.description: The line the finding is on. 0 when it is on no line of a file: the pull request's body, a file that is missing.

grade.description: critical: wrong data, a security hole, lost work, something published unapproved. major: a person is misled or stuck — an untrue screen, a dead control, a failure shown as success. minor: polish — spacing, wording, a small visual slip. nit: taste.

tag.description: important: a defect this change introduces or re-exposes. nit: taste, style or cleanup, always graded nit and dropped. pre-existing: a defect in code this change did not introduce; it never blocks, never goes back to the builder and is never filed as a ticket: the driver sends it to the nightly sweep.

verified.description: The verifier agent's own word on this finding, copied, never worked out: confirmed, plausible, or unverified when no verifier judged it (a gap-sweep addition). A refuted one is not returned. The driver derives the tally from it: confirmed is its finder and its verifier agreeing (2 of 2), plausible 1 of 2, unverified 1 of 1.

verifier.description: The description of the verifier agent that judged this finding, copied exactly as it was started (e.g. "Verify: avg empty list NaN"). The driver reads that agent's own verdict off the transcript; `verified` is only the fallback.

votes.description: The tally of agents that judged this finding: of = how many judged it, agree = how many held it real. With `verified` the driver derives it and ignores what is typed here. The driver keeps only a finding a majority agree on, and at least review.quorum (default 2).

class.description: When the finding is a class of mistake rather than one slip, the class in a few words. The fix step fixes every instance, not only this line.

instances.description: Every place the class occurs, as file:line, this finding's own place included.

reason.description: One line, in a user's words, saying why this grade. A Critical or a Major names who is harmed and how; a grade with no harm behind it is a Minor wearing a blocker's label.

question.description: Why this step cannot finish. Answerable in a line: a yes/no or a pick.

questionKind.description: What kind of question it is. `base-red`: a red that fails the same way at the merge base. `uncommitted-fix`: the change passes but is not committed. `already-fixed`: the ask already holds on the integration branch. `uat-data`: it wants UAT or production data. `other`: anything else. Never ask for UAT or production data: measure on the local seed or the fixtures, and say so in the pull request.

questionFor.description: Who answers the question. `owner`: pixels, a picture, a product or commercial call, or the data model. `pm`: the ticket's shape — which repo, how it splits, the order, the wording of its acceptance. Unsure is `owner`; the driver treats anything but `pm` as the owner's.
